observation.visible_scene: A clear tapered glass tumbler sits on a dark reflective surface against a smooth gray gradient backdrop. The glass holds two stratified liquids: a dark brown/black layer filling the lower portion and a translucent amber/orange layer above, separated by a reddish-orange interface band. A bright orange wedge/slice is submerged, pressed against the right inner wall of the glass. Fine suspended specks and small bubbles are visible throughout the upper amber layer.
visible_changes: The submerged orange wedge gradually shifts downward and rotates, moving from a steeply angled position on the upper right in the early frames to a flatter, more horizontal orientation lower in the glass by the final frames.
The reddish-orange interface band between the two liquid layers slowly descends and flattens, becoming more horizontal and lower in the glass toward the end of the excerpt.
Small particles and bubbles within the amber layer drift and reconfigure over time, indicating gentle internal motion/settling.
The glass outline, rim position, and background remain fixed relative to the frame, indicating the camera is static and the observed motion is internal to the contents rather than camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the layering and of the wedge's placement/sinking is not shown.
Whether the wedge was added before this segment or how it arrived at its initial position is unseen.
The final resting state of the wedge and the eventual mixing or separation of the layers lie beyond the cropped segment.
uncertain_details: The exact direction and magnitude of the interface-band movement are subtle and could partly reflect changes in the wedge's occlusion rather than pure liquid displacement.
It is not possible to confirm whether the speck motion represents rising, sinking, or random drift.
No contact event, onset, or completion is visible; the settling/mixing process is already underway at the first frame and continues past the last.
